newsitem.title: CUBA: CUBA, HONDURAS TAKE FIRST STEP TO DIPLOMATIC TIES.
newsitem.headline: CUBA, HONDURAS TAKE FIRST STEP TO DIPLOMATIC TIES.

text.p: Cuba and Honduras have agreed to open "interests offices" in each other's capitals as a first step towards renewing diplomatic relations, the Cuban government said on Wednesday.
The Foreign Ministry said in a statement that the move was a "prelude to the restoration of full diplomatic relations."
Details of setting up the interests offices -- diplomatic missions that fall short of being full embassies -- would be worked out in the coming weeks, it said.
Honduras broke relations with Cuba in April 1961, like many Latin American nations that sought to isolate Cuba after President Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution.

In central America, the communist-ruled island now has full diplomatic relations with Nicaragua, Panama and Belize, and an interests office in Costa Rica. It has no relations with Guatemala and El Salvador.
